steps.text: Wall St & Broad St · Financial District · 2:52 PM

sub: Mr. Marin, a pizza chain in its fifth year is a risk profile, not a business.
It's twelve stores. People love it. There's a pizza with a fried egg.
Which is precisely the risk. Have a pleasant afternoon.

lines: Don't talk. Listen. I'm at the school. Milo's not here.
What do you mean not here. It's two fifty.
Ms. Okafor says a nanny signed him out at two fifteen. Family emergency.
I KNOW we don't have a nanny, John. She had a nanny haircut. White hair. Cardigan. Very professional.
Then my phone buzzes. Unknown number. A photo of Milo eating fries. And a name.
...Okay. Okay. I'm getting in the car.
Don't you dare hang up on me. Not today. Not once today.
I won't. I'm putting you on the car.

voicemail.text: John Marin, if you send me to voicemail today of all days, I will haunt you. Call me back. It's Milo.

steps.text: One million. 10 PM. You'll be told where. No cops, planner. Pickup time.
One million. I have... a pizza chain and eleven thousand dollars.

steps.name: safe
steps.label: SAFE PICKUP

steps.text: boss the armored truck just pulled out of wall st. it's on your map. beat it here or the safe goes to the bank

lines: Okay. Breathing. I'm breathing. Where are you going?
The ATM, then the first store. The safe has the week's take.
An ATM. For a ransom. You're going to get two hundred dollars and a receipt.
Oh, two thousand, great, we'll get him back in installments.
The armored truck takes the safe at three oh five. I can beat it.
Then beat it. Drive like we used to drive. Not like a dad.
I drive like a dad because I'm a dad.
Not today, you're not. Today you're a getaway with a car seat.
extra: I should have been here at two. The meeting was at two. I moved it.
Nails. I moved our son's teacher meeting for nails, John.
If you'd been there at two, she'd have come at one. They planned this. It's not the nails.
Don't be nice to me right now. I can't do nice. Be mean.
I can hear them. They sound terrible.
...Thank you. That helped. That's sick, but it helped.
He took his walkie-talkie to school today. The dinosaur one.
The one that beeps at three in the morning?
That's the one. I hated it. I'd give anything to hear it beep right now.
Did you tell her? Your mother?
How do I tell my mother her grandson is... no. Not yet.
Fine. But when she finds out, I'm telling her you knew first.
wrap: The store's ahead. I can see the sign.
SLICE MARIN. In letters you can see from space. We may as well have put up a map.
It's a confession with a logo.
Go. Get the money. I'm getting in my car. I can't sit at a school gate looking at the swings.

pause: CARISSA MARIN
Hold on. Your other line's lit. It says MA. Take it, or she'll call me.
resume: Ricotta. She wants to know about ricotta.

lines: Johnny! It's your mother. Are you eating? You sound like you're driving.
Sunday. Lasagna. Does Milo still hate ricotta or was that a phase?
Ma, it's not a good time.
It's never a good time with you. Your father had a good time once. Nineteen eighty-one.
He told me he hates it. Last week. To my face. Put him on.
He's... at school. I'll call you back.
You never call back. Kiss him for me.

voicemail.text: Johnny, it's your mother. Call me. It's about ricotta.

lines: Boss, it's Benny. The truck's early, it's at Worth already, I'm stalling him with a calzone. Hurry.

steps.text: Two thousand. Zero point two percent of a kid.

steps.name: lou
steps.label: LOU LEAVES

sub: Johnny Marin. You still put pineapple on the pies?
Lou, I need a hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Today.
For that I need collateral. The chain.

steps.prompt: Lou wants the chain as collateral.

reply: Lou Varga
Pleasure. And Johnny? Thin crust is a cry for help.
Lou Varga
Fine, the Tribeca store stays yours. You just cost yourself twenty seconds.

lines: School says she signed out as A. Teodoro. Family friend.
She knew the password, John. Pepperoni.
How did it go with Lou? Did you have to sign anything?
Our chain. The whole thing. To a man who calls me 'sweetheart cakes'.
He gave us a hundred and fifty.
John. You sound well. Pizza agrees with you.
He's eating ice cream. I'm not a monster. I'm an accountant who got robbed.
Five years ago you emptied my boat and my life. Now you pay it back. With interest, I'm being kind.
Put him on. I want to hear him.
He doesn't want to talk to you. Here. Say something to your father.

voicemail.text: You don't pick up? I have your son's backpack. Pick up.

lines: He just pressed his little toy. Twice. Children. Ten o'clock, John.
And John? Tell the school to send the police home. Or I'll know.
Look in your mirror. My friends are saying hello.
What did he say? You went quiet. You never go quiet.
He put Milo on. He didn't talk. He pressed his walkie twice.
Two beeps. Two beeps means he's okay. That's our game. Me and him.
We have a whole language, John, you work late.
Are those horns yours? Are you being chased? Already?
Two black cars. Very polite. Very fast.
Take Chambers. No, the other Chambers. There's only one Chambers. TAKE IT.
You used to lose cops in a minivan with a mattress on the roof.
extra: The school called the police. The headmaster called me after he called you.
Then he's watching the school. Which means he's watching me. Good.
Let him watch. I'm the scariest thing at that school and that includes the lunch lady.
Is it bad that I'm a little bit proud of how fast you're driving?
wrap: Quiet? You lost them? Look at you. My husband the felon.
Former felon. Current hero. Go to Tribeca, Benny has the van.

pause: CARISSA MARIN
You got out. I'll hold. I'm eating your fries.
resume: There you are. Where were we? Oh right. Crisis.

lines: Mr. Marin. Lionel Ashby, Head of School. I'm so sorry to call under these circumstances.
Procedure requires me to inform you we've notified the police. A detective is on her way.
No. You can't. Call them off.
I can't 'call off' the police, Mr. Marin. That's rather the point of them.
Is there a reason you'd prefer they weren't involved? A custody matter, perhaps?
There's no custody matter. We're married. Happily. Mostly.
Then the detective will help. Her name is Calloway. She's very thorough.

voicemail.text: Mr. Marin, this is Lionel Ashby, Head of School. Please return my call. It's procedural, and urgent.

steps.text: One fifty. That's a whole Lou.

missions.timerLine: Every register before the bank sweep.

lines: Boss, keys are in the visor. Don't touch the big slice, it's held on with hope.
Benny, I need every register. Cash only.
Every register? Boss, are we getting robbed? Are WE robbing?
Nobody's robbing. It's a... family thing.
My uncle said that once. Then we didn't see him for eighteen months. Okay. Cash. I'll call ahead.

voicemail.text: Boss, it's Benny. Keys are in the visor. Call me.

steps.text: Franklin Street register. Thirteen. Smells like garlic and bad decisions.

steps.name: sweep
steps.label: BANK SWEEP

lines: Okay, I made a spreadsheet. Don't laugh.
You were the spreadsheet guy. I'm the spreadsheet guy now. Column B is 'things we can sell'.
Your watch. My ring. The good blender.
Nobody pays a ransom with a blender.
It's a very good blender, John.
extra: There's a pizza on the roof. A big plastic slice. It whistles over thirty.
Our brand whistles. I love that for us.
Okay, he's eating. That's good. That's... I'm going to be sick.
Pull over? No. Don't pull over. Keep going. I'll be sick for both of us.
Do you need me to talk?
Yes. Talk. Say anything. Tell me about the van.
It smells like garlic and somebody's left a whole pepperoni roll under the seat.
Eat it anyway. You haven't eaten since breakfast. I know you.
Milo wanted to be a delivery driver when he grew up. Then an astronaut. Then a tree.
He said trees don't have homework. He's not wrong.
I keep thinking we should call the detective. Tell her everything.
Everything? Carissa. 'Everything' is five years and three states.
I know what everything is. I was there for most of it. I drove for most of it.
Then you know what happens to Milo's parents if we tell her everything.
...I hate when you're right in that voice.
The planner voice. It's back. I hate it. Don't stop.

pause: CARISSA MARIN
It's beeping. Who is it? Take it, take it.
resume: He says Milo's eating bread. Crusts off. No butter.

I had a family business. You remember. Boats. Warehouses. A man with a parrot.
Now I have one office and a boy who only eats bread with the crusts cut off.
Plain. He likes it plain. No butter.
We know. He told us. Very firmly. He's your wife's son.

voicemail.text: You don't pick up? I have your son's backpack. Pick up.

John. Is this how we get him back? Stealing and selling and running? Like before?
It's how we get the money. Getting him back is something else.
extra: The guy's phone said uptown by four.
Uptown. Uptown's huge. Uptown's half the island. That narrows it to... uptown.
It means not Brooklyn, not Jersey, not a boat. He kept him here.
He kept him close. Why would he keep him close?
Because he wants to watch us come to him.
What else, then? Getting him back.

One twenty-five. Three sixty-five total. We're a third of a kid.

reply: Agnes Teodoro
A man named Rollo took him at Rivington. He complained about an elevator. An office uptown, on the big street with the old theater sign.
Agnes Teodoro

steps.text: A man named Rollo took him at Rivington. An office uptown, on the big street with the old theater sign.

That's my son. Teddy. Oh, Teddy, no.

steps.name: teddy
steps.label: TEDDY'S PHONE

lines: You're tailing a nanny's son. In a black sports car. Very subtle.

Don't shh me, I'm not in the car. I'm three avenues away eating a granola bar for strength.

It means you didn't tell me the painting was still in the store. For five years.
I didn't want you to worry.
I'm worrying NOW, John! Retroactively! It's very efficient!
Yes. After. I'm writing it on my other hand.
Is he still ahead of you? Don't get close. You always get close.
Make it a block and a half. Half blocks are where people get caught.
John. Did she say if he cried? When she took him?

He asked about YOU. Not me. I do pickup every day, and he asked about you.
Because I'm never at pickup. He thought something was wrong.
That's the saddest compliment I've ever heard. For both of us.

Forsyth. Okay. Don't go in alone. ...You're going in alone. Of course you are.

pause: CARISSA MARIN
Your phone's lit up. Take it, but don't lose him.
resume: Ashby. The detective's asking if we have 'a history'.

I'm writing them down. I've got a crayon and a juice box and I'm writing them down.

extra: Delgado called. He said Milo fell asleep on his coat.

That man has my son asleep on his coat and I'm in traffic on Second Avenue.
I'm fine. I'm not fine. I'm going to bite the steering wheel. Keep driving.
Did he say anything else? About Miami?
Good. No. Not good. I don't know. Don't make me feel sorry for him.
I'm not. I'm just telling you what he said.
You always do this. You understand the bad guy. You did it with the parrot man.
wrap: Lost them? Okay. Washington Square. Bunny wants to see you.

pause: CARISSA MARIN

resume: There you are. Where were we? Oh right. Crisis.

Don't. You're not sorry. You're a planner. You're planning while you say it.
Your boy fell asleep. On my coat.

voicemail.text: You don't pick up? I have your son's backpack. Pick up.

Sorry. Not sorry. Tired. Washington Square.

pause: CARISSA MARIN

resume: There you are. Where were we? Oh right. Crisis.

That's not a plan. That's a hope with a spreadsheet.
Meaning I'm in a car doing nothing while you collect for a woman named after a rabbit.

You got out. I'll hold. I'm eating your fries.

Johnny. A policewoman called me. At home. Asking about you.

Something's wrong. I can hear it. You sounded like this when you were nine and the hamster.
I'm making the lasagna. I'm making it now. Bring him home to eat it. You hear me?

voicemail.text: Johnny, it's your mother. A policewoman called the house. Call me back. I'm making the lasagna.

steps.text: One hundred and eighty thousand dollars. In my trunk. Next to the spare.

lines: Are those sirens? Are those YOUR sirens?

extra: Calloway called me. My mother gave her my number.
Your MOTHER. Your mother talked to a detective?
